title: Open restriction and adjunction transport through actual completion units
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$ use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], $B_{n,T}=(A_n)_T$ and $\widehat R_T=\lim_nB_{n,T}$. Use the strict semilinear module-system category $\mathscr S_T$, derived reduction $\mathcal R_T\dashv\mathcal L_T$, and the actual unit $u$ and counit $e$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Completeness means the quotient-tower Roos-triangle condition of [def-weil-derived-complete], and normalized means that every transition-adjoint $N_m\otimes^L_{B_{m,T}}B_{n,T}\to N_n$ is invertible for $m\ge n$. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Identify $j^{-1}\widehat R_X=\widehat R_U$ and $j^{-1}B_{n,X}=B_{n,U}$. Write $j_!\dashv j^*$ for exact localized ringed-site extension and restriction, $J_j\dashv P_j$ for their termwise-system adjunctions, and $\eta^o,\epsilon^o,\eta^S,\epsilon^S$ for the respective units and counits [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

Assume that $j_!$ preserves quotient-complete objects and that the actual $u_P$ is invertible on every quotient-complete object on $U$ and $X$, while $e_N$ is invertible on normalized systems and $\mathcal L_TN$ is complete for such $N$. Supply a natural isomorphism $r_K:\mathcal R_Xj_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}J_j\mathcal R_UK$ represented simultaneously on flat-term K-flat complexes by the canonical open tensor maps $[x]\otimes a\mapsto[x\otimes a|_U]$, commuting with strict quotient transitions and scalar-unit augmentations [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

Ordinary restriction $j^*$ preserves quotient completeness and agrees with completed restriction, including its actual completion comparison and finite projections [lem-sf-immersion-completed-pullback-comparison]. Restriction of the quotient tensor models defines a natural strict-system isomorphism
$$s_H:\mathcal R_Uj^*H\xrightarrow{\sim}P_j\mathcal R_XH.$$
For every complete $K$ on $U$ and complete $H$ on $X$, the following are equalities of the specified simultaneous derived system transformations:
$$P_j(r_K)\circ s_{j_!K}\circ\mathcal R_U(\eta^o_K)=\eta^S_{\mathcal R_UK},$$
$$\mathcal R_X(\epsilon^o_H)=\epsilon^S_{\mathcal R_XH}\circ J_j(s_H)\circ r_{j^*H}.$$
Define
$$d_K=u_{j_!K}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_X(r_K^{-1}),\qquad
 b_H=u_{j^*H}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_U(s_H^{-1}).$$
These are natural isomorphisms, and their normalization and realized-adjunction equations are
$$r_K\circ\mathcal R_X(d_K)=e_{J_j\mathcal R_UK},$$
$$b_{j_!K}\circ\mathcal L_U(P_j(r_K^{-1}))\circ\mathcal L_U(\eta^S_{\mathcal R_UK})\circ u_K=\eta^o_K,$$
$$u_H^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_X(\epsilon^S_{\mathcal R_XH})\circ\mathcal L_X(J_j(s_H))\circ d_{j^*H}^{-1}=\epsilon^o_H.$$
In particular $d$ and $b$ identify the realized open adjunction with the localized ringed-site adjunction. The equalities hold before evaluating the systems, and use the actual adjunction units, counits and transposes rather than arbitrary reconstruction isomorphisms.

proof.text: Apply lem-sf-canonical-open-restriction-model to the supplied tensor comparison and its ExtensionModel to obtain s, its restriction representatives, and its equality with the mate of r inverse. The unit_mateEquiv and mateEquiv_counit equations, composed with r, give the two reduced adjunction equations for all ambient objects.

Apply lem-sf-open-restriction-completeness to obtain hc and invertibility of the actual completion unit. CompletionModel follows separately from completionUnit_existsUnique, naturality along the exact-functor representative isomorphism and mappingCocone.lift_fst; composing with the first Roos projection gives every quotient augmentation.

Define di and bi by the displayed inverse-unit formulas. Build their natural isomorphisms pointwise; naturality is unit naturality followed by the naturality of r or s. For normalization use inv(R.map unit)=counit and counit naturality. Substitute bi into the realized unit equation and use the reduced unit equation to cancel the comparison maps. Unit naturality gives the result. For the counit, the inverse of di is unit followed by the limit image of r; combine consecutive limit images and use the reduced counit equation, then unit naturality and cancellation of its inverse.
